findings.disposition_rationale: peer-cred.js added to the default code-custody closure.
Repo custody covers the gitfile, working-tree root, git dirs and (when present) their config files.
status vets git, gh and the repository before calling them; skipped conditions report unknown with a named reason.
origin host must be github.com or ssh.github.com; the PR head is checked against the pushed commit; mismatch closes the PR and refuses pr-head-mismatch.
checked_at printed outside the fence only when ISO-UTC.
Trust-file write refuses symlinks and uses O_NOFOLLOW.
An absent config.worktree no longer reads as runner-writable (regression introduced and fixed in this PR).
PR view/close only on a validated github.com PR URL for the target repo.
ssh.github.com accepted; repo-mismatch detail names the host; spec updated.
Every repo config file is an optional leaf checked only when present, so linked worktrees are not refused.
The runner cannot change origin: the custody check refuses a runner-writable .git, config or working tree, and the PR-head check ties the PR to the pushed commit.
pin trusts the human's own global git config and environment; the runner cannot write them, and every git call disables hooks.
The --dry-run detail shows the base branch's trust file, which is human-approved content, printed to the human's terminal.
Lazily loaded modules (peer-cred) were added to the closure in an earlier pass, with a test on the real default.
Deleting the pin branch on a failed PR create can remove a same-named branch from an earlier pin run for the same key; it holds only that pin commit.
The reviewer withdrew the local-ref ready_to_count finding itself.
runner_identity reads the human's own gh login, which is the input the spec defines.
The fingerprint comes from a validated identify reply checked against the key before it is written.
An unresolvable ancestor is treated as writable, so host checks fail closed.
